draft.title: The Industrial Revolution in brief
card: The Industrial Revolution began in Britain from about 1750. Before it, most goods were made by hand, often at home or in small workshops.
Over the next decades, machines took over much of this work. Machines were large and costly, so they were housed in factories, where many workers ran them.
Factories needed many workers, so many people left farms and villages to find jobs. Towns grew quickly into large cities.
So the change had two sides: how goods were made shifted from hand to machine, and where people lived and worked shifted from the countryside to the city.
draft.remember: Hand to machine, and countryside to city: Britain from about 1750.

a.q: Which change best describes the start of the Industrial Revolution in Britain?
opts: Goods began to be made by machines in factories
Goods began to be made by hand in small workshops
Farm work began to replace factory work in cities
Britain began to stop trading goods with other places
a.why: The Industrial Revolution was a move from hand production to machines housed in factories. Making goods by hand in workshops describes the way things were done before it, so it is the reverse of the change.
a.clue: Think about what changed from the way goods were made before 1750.

b.q: In 1820, Tom leaves his family's farm in a village in northern England and takes a job running a machine in a large factory. Why does Tom's move fit the Industrial Revolution?
opts: Factories needed many workers, so people moved to towns
Farms had been banned, so people had to move to towns
Hand work had grown, so people moved to towns to find it
Towns were small and quiet, so people moved there for peace
b.why: Machines in factories needed many workers, and this drew people from the countryside to find jobs in growing towns and cities. Hand work did not grow: machines took over much of it, so the third option has the change the wrong way round.
b.clue: Ask what factories needed in order to run their machines.

a.best: Goods began to be made by machines in factories

b.best: Factories needed many workers, so people moved to towns
